title: two Error classes whose durable contract identities differ compile and reach the plan as one action, on both backends
notes: The negative control for `two-error-classes-whose-durable-identities-collide-are-rejected`, and it exists because this project has shipped six over-corrections. That refusal case now declares SMITHERS4124 and a `messageContains` naming both colliding class names; this case declares neither, and that asymmetry is the point — a diagnostic precise enough to name two classes is also a diagnostic that can be made to fire on two classes that do not collide, and the only thing that would catch that is a program with two Error classes in one channel that must still compile. This is that program. It is byte-for-byte that case with `$Failed` renamed to `Failed` and `_Failed` renamed to `Denied` — nothing else differs, so the ONLY thing separating a refusal from a clean compile is whether the two durable contract identities collide. A collision check that fires on any two Error classes in a failure channel, rather than only on two that normalize to one identity, turns this case red instead of passing quietly, which is the failure mode a refusal-only case cannot detect. This is also the first case in the corpus that exercises an Action failure channel and RUNS on both backends. It was written when `an-actions-failure-channel-mints-one-identity-per-error-class` scored `unsupported` on the Go fork — that case reads `errorSchema.descriptor`, and the fork emitted a stub error schema that had no `descriptor` field — so this program, which observes only `Flow.plan.actions.length`, was the only place the compile-and-run half of the failure-channel contract could be measured on both sides. Since 2026-08-28 the fork derives the error schema and that case passes on both backends too, so this one is no longer the only such row; it remains the narrower observation, which is why it is kept. What the single stdout line means: the flow lowers to exactly one action descriptor, so the two-variant failure channel neither split the action nor dropped it. VERIFIED LOAD-BEARING, not assumed: mutating the declared stdout from ['1'] to ['2'] turns the case red on BOTH backends with the stdout diff printed, and the file was restored. This case pins CURRENT behaviour — it passed before the Go identity fix and after it, which is the point: that fix added a refusal beside the benign path and must not have moved the benign path.
